title: Electronics Sellers: How to Photograph Screens, Reflections, and Black Products That Sell
description: Photographing electronics is hard—reflections, screens, and black surfaces all fight you. Here's the workflow that works.

blocks.text: Electronics photography is the hardest professional discipline. Every surface reflects. Every screen fights your lighting. Black plastic swallows detail. And buyers demand crystal-clear specs before spending real money.
Here's the workflow that solves all three problems.
The Reflection Problem
Metal, glass, and glossy plastic reflect your entire room—your camera, your face, your ceiling light. Amateur electronics photos always give it away.
Fix: Diffuse your light source aggressively. A bedsheet or paper diffuser between your lamp and the product eliminates 80% of reflections. What remains, edit out later.
The Black Product Problem
Black electronics photographed on white backgrounds turn into featureless silhouettes. Buyers can't see edges, buttons, or detail.

Use edit-photo to remove the background and export a transparent PNG. Create white or branded layout versions with the site's supported main-image workflow or a separate design editor; capture and color correction still need to be handled before or after background removal.
The Screen Problem
Turned-off screens look dead. Turned-on screens create weird lighting. Photoshopped screens look fake.
Export a transparent PNG from edit-photo, then place it into the final scene or layout with a general design editor. Keep the original and transparent master so the composition remains reversible.
The Cable Nightmare
Every phone, laptop, and gadget photo has cables snaking somewhere. They look messy and unprofessional.

If a source image contains a watermark, obtain an unwatermarked file from the rights holder or create your own photo. edit-photo does not remove watermarks, and removing ownership marks without permission can create legal and marketplace risks.

Marketplace-Specific Optimization

Amazon: Pure white background, product 85% of frame.
Best Buy Marketplace: White background, no props.
eBay: Neutral gray or white acceptable.
Your own Shopify: Lifestyle scenes—laptop on a desk, phone in a hand.
